citation: Drummond, K. V., Tucker-Bradway, N., Smith, D.-M., Hubbard, D., Meakin, J., & Salinger, T. (2020). Children's Literacy Initiative: Final Report of the i3 Scale-Up Study. Washington, DC: American Institutes for Research.
report_number: AIR i3 Scale-Up Final Report (Sep 2020); ERIC ED610842
design: RCT; school-level cluster random assignment (within 12 blocks across 4 urban districts: Broward FL, Denver CO, Elizabeth NJ, Houston TX); 55 schools randomized (27 treatment / 28 control), 54 analytic after one Denver treatment school dropped out (26 T / 28 C); subject = Reading/literacy; grades K-3 (followed up to Grade 5 on state tests); low-SES, high-EL schools. TPD = Children's Literacy Initiative (CLI) structured literacy intervention: 3 years of teacher training seminars, coaching, instructional-lead-teacher mentoring, and leader meetings, vs business-as-usual literacy instruction/PD (control schools received a small book-purchase stipend).
problems: The report reports student-achievement effect sizes (ES = average treatment effect / pooled within-group SD from a 3-level HLM, ITT, pretest- and covariate-adjusted) together with two-tailed t-test p-values and sample sizes, but it does NOT report standard errors or the standardizing SDs as numeric values. I therefore recorded the reported ES directly as the standardized impact (d) and derived g = J*d. impact_se / g_se were back-computed from the reported (rounded, 3-dp) p-value via se = |ES| / z, z = Phi^-1(1 - p/2). These SEs already embody the HLM cluster adjustment (they are far larger than a naive student-level no-cluster variance, as expected for a school-randomized design), so cluster_adjusted=true. Because p is rounded and (for these null results) large, the back-computed SE/variance is approximate; for very large p the inverse-normal is sensitive to rounding. No ICC is reported in the document, so icc is left null (not guessed). Both achievement results are null (not statistically significant in any year). The report's headline conclusion is that CLI had no significant impact on student reading achievement. End-of-treatment wave (Year 3) extracted as the primary records; earlier-year waves and entry-grade subgroups are described in notes (not extracted as separate rows except where they are the only full-sample estimate). The Grade-1-entry subgroup showed notably larger ESs (GRADE ES ~.14-.15 in Years 2-3; State ELA ES .118 in Year 3) but these are non-randomised grade subgroups and were not statistically significant in the primary analysis.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Children's Literacy Initiative (CLI) structured literacy PD vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.grade_band: Grades 2-3 (students who entered the study in K/Grade 1 and were in Grades 2-3 by Year 3; pooled across grades)
effect_sizes.test_name: GRADE (Group Reading Assessment and Diagnostic Evaluation), total/overall scale score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of treatment, Year 3 / 2018-19, the final intervention year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report gives the standardized impact directly: ES = average treatment effect (3-level HLM, students in classrooms in schools, block fixed effects, ITT, adjusted for baseline GRADE pretest + student covariates) divided by the pooled within-group SD of the outcome (Table 8). Treated this ES = d = 0.041. Hedges' g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1947, J = 0.999615; g = 0.040984. SE back-computed from the reported two-tailed t-test p = 0.580: z = Phi^-1(1 - 0.580/2) = 0.5534, se_d = |0.041|/0.5534 = 0.07409; g_se = J*se_d = 0.074057; g_var = g_se^2. This SE reflects the HLM cluster adjustment.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 8, p. 19 (physical p. 27); methods p. 13-14 (physical p. 21-22)
effect_sizes.notes: GRADE total score pooled across grades, full analytic sample. Year 3 is the end-of-treatment wave (extracted). Other waves: Year 1 (Grades K-3) ES = -0.005, p=0.894, n=5,659 (T=2,792/C=2,867); Year 2 (Grades 1-3) ES = 0.010, p=0.861, n=3,409 (T=1,664/C=1,745). None statistically significant. The GRADE was administered to a randomly selected subset (~40 students per grade per school) of English-proficient students; the Year-3 pooled sample is smaller because earlier entry-grade cohorts aged out of testing (students reaching Grade 4 left the GRADE pool). Entry-grade breakdown (Table 9, non-randomised subgroups, not extracted as separate rows): Year 3 ES by entry grade = Kindergarten -0.050 (p=0.582), Grade 1 +0.144 (p=0.092); Grades 2/3 aged out. SE derived from rounded p-value; approximate.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Children's Literacy Initiative (CLI) structured literacy PD vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.grade_band: Grade 3+ (state ELA tested; all students reaching Grade 3+ by Year 3, pooled across entry grades)
effect_sizes.test_name: State standardized end-of-year ELA assessments (FSA-Florida, CMAS-Colorado, STAAR-Texas, PARCC/NJSLA-New Jersey), standardized within state/grade/year to mean 0, SD 1
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of treatment, Year 3 / 2018-19, the final intervention year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Report gives the standardized impact directly: ES = average treatment effect (same 3-level HLM, ITT, pretest/covariate-adjusted) on state ELA scores that were first normalized within state/grade/year to mean 0 SD 1; the ES is the HLM impact divided by the pooled within-group SD (Table 10, 'All students' row). Treated this ES = d = 0.018. Hedges' g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 8557, J = 0.999912; g = 0.017998. SE back-computed from the reported two-tailed p = 0.772: z = Phi^-1(1 - 0.772/2) = 0.2898, se_d = |0.018|/0.2898 = 0.06212; g_se = J*se_d = 0.062110; g_var = g_se^2. Reflects HLM cluster adjustment.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 10, p. 21 (physical p. 29); methods p. 13-14 (physical p. 21-22)
effect_sizes.notes: State ELA, 'All students' (full sample pooled across entry grades), Year 3 = end-of-treatment wave (extracted). Other waves for 'All students': Year 1 n/a (only Grade 3 students had state-test data in Year 1, so no all-students total); Year 2 ES = 0.007, p=0.905, n=6,514 (T=2,981/C=3,533). Year 3 ES = 0.018, p=0.772, n=8,559 (T=3,948/C=4,611). Not statistically significant. State tests start in Grade 3, so this sample is the cumulative pool of students who had reached Grade 3+ by the given year (it grows across years and is larger than the GRADE subset). Entry-grade breakdown (Table 10, non-randomised subgroups, not extracted as separate rows): Year 3 ES by entry grade = Grade 1 +0.118 (p=0.102), Grade 2 -0.033 (p=0.698), Grade 3 -0.069 (p=0.536). SE derived from rounded p-value; approximate.
